Detail

Cincinnati Reds @ Chicago Cubs, 4:20p

Summary

Chase Burns pitching against a shaky Cubs bullpen at Wrigley is appointment viewing, and the gNERD score backs it up. At 15.61, this game sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historical 95th percentile, with Burns' 10.25 pNERD leading all pitchers on the board.

Cincinnati hands the ball to Chase Burns, who carries a 14-3 record and a 2.77 ERA, a 1.15 WHIP and 10.6 strikeouts per nine across 25 starts, backed by a 3.11 FIP, and his 97.7 mph average velocity and elite whiff rate explain why the 23-year-old is drawing Cy Young buzz. Imanaga is respectable if unspectacular — a 6.08 pNERD — though he's coming off the shortest start of his major league career, so watch for an early hook. The Cubs' offense and defense (10.42 tNERD, boosted by standout fielding and batting runs) make them the far stronger club on paper, while Cincinnati's bullpen and lineup lag behind. Series context adds spice too: the first two games were loud, with Cincinnati winning 10-8 Friday before Chicago answered with a 17-5 rout in which Pete Crow-Armstrong homered three times. Wild-card stakes for Chicago make this rubber match matter beyond the pitching duel.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ St. Louis Cardinals, 11:15a

Summary

A dominant Pirates arm riding a historic hot streak faces a Cardinals lefty who's quietly beating his peripherals — this one's worth carving out time for. Braxton Ashcraft has been the story of the summer in Pittsburgh: he recently threw the 16th complete game of the season, needing just 85 pitches to get through all nine innings, averaging fewer than ten pitches per frame, and became the first pitcher in MLB history to throw 9 innings with 10+ strikeouts on 85 or fewer pitches. That gem wasn't a one-off — he's notched his third consecutive quality start, giving up exactly one run in each of his past three outings for a 1.17 ERA across 23 innings. His 11.62 pNERD is comfortably above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile, backed by plus velocity, elite strike-throwing, and a sharp xFIP-. Liberatore is a more modest complement (6.44 pNERD), buoyed largely by a hefty positive luck figure suggesting his results have been better than his run-prevention peripherals so far. Team-wise, both clubs are middling — Pittsburgh's baserunning and bullpen give it a slight edge, while St. Louis leans on defense and a young, cheap roster. The 15.28 gNERD sits well above both the historic and today's averages, making Ashcraft's start the headline reason to tune in.

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 9:15a

Summary

Here's my summary:

A high-scoring lineup battle with two lively teams but two underwhelming starters — watch for the offense, not the pitching. Both clubs bring surprisingly solid tNERD marks (Marlins 9.44, Nationals 8.66) built on youth, aggressive baserunning, and payroll thrift, pushing the gNERD to 12.88, comfortably above the historic median and right around today's slate average.

The storylines are plentiful: this is the finale of a three-game set in which the Nationals won the opener 9-2 on Friday night and 5-4 in 10 innings on Saturday, and Washington has scored 718 runs in 2026, trailing the MLB-leading Chicago Cubs by just two — this is a lineup that hits. Andrew Alvarez takes the mound looking to snap a personal skid; he's seeking to break his personal three-game losing streak, though the record undersells him, backed by a tidy 91 xFIP- and the highest pNERD on the slate at 5.10. Janson Junk is the weaker link statistically (pNERD 2.56, dreadful swinging-strike rate), and he's on short rest, making his third appearance in eight days after already beating this same Nationals lineup last Sunday. Bullpens on both sides are gassed from the series, so don't be surprised if this turns into another slugfest rather than a pitcher's duel — the teams, not the arms, are what make this one worth a look.

Texas Rangers @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

This is a good find - Dustin May's health status is a real storyline. Let me write the summary now.

Milwaukee's got the better team and the better story, but Dustin May's health is the actual headline here. The Brewers, riding an 85-51 record and gunning for a series sweep, throw out a lineup that's produced the best all-around tNERD score in this matchup (10.32) thanks to strong baserunning, a deep bullpen, and a young, cost-efficient roster — genuinely one of the more watchable teams in baseball right now. But May's turn in the rotation comes with real uncertainty: he threw one pitch on Aug. 26 against the Mets before a 106 mph line drive struck him, and left that game, with soreness reported, though he played catch the next day and the club pointed to Sunday as a possible return. When healthy his stuff plays — 96.8 mph average velocity drives a strong pNERD of 5.97 — but his last real outing wasn't pretty, as his last full outing was rough too, with Seattle scoring seven off him on Aug. 19 before the third inning ended. Rocker, opposite him, has had genuine swing-and-miss stretches (a record that undersells his recent work, striking out eight over 5 2/3 innings in an 11-2 win at the White Sox on Aug. 24) but his control remains shaky. At a gNERD of 12.83, this sits comfortably above the historical average and near today's slate average — worth a look, but watch the injury report before first pitch.

Boston Red Sox @ New York Yankees, 10:35a

Summary

Have a great sense of the storylines now. Let me write the summary.

A rubber match with a real prize on the line: this Red Sox-Yankees finale carries a season-series tiebreaker and, potentially, playoff seeding implications. After Boston and New York split the first two games of this set (a Red Sox blowout followed by a Yankees rout), the two AL East rivals enter the series finale deadlocked after Boston had held a season-long lead in the head-to-head series, with the winner earning a tiebreaker advantage. That context alone should elevate the stakes above a typical Sunday getaway game. The gNERD of 12.83 sits a bit above the historical average of 10.81, and above today's slate average too, driven mostly by the Yankees' tNERD of 7.81 — New York ranks 3rd in the league for home runs (184) despite a light contact profile. On the mound, Ranger Suarez brings a strong xFIP-driven pNERD of 5.88, while Will Warren counters with a modest 5.01, buoyed by youth and some positive regression expected. Warren has curiously become second on the Yankees in wins this year despite unremarkable peripherals, so don't expect his win total to tell you much about how he'll actually pitch. Worth catching for the stakes, not necessarily the artistry.

Chicago White Sox @ Minnesota Twins, 11:10a

Summary

Jordan Hicks moonlighting as an opener throwing 99 mph, plus a Twins team quietly circling the drain defensively — there's enough weirdness here to make this one worth a look. The White Sox arrive riding a four-game winning streak and are on a four-game surge and lead the season series 6-3, while Minnesota is trying to avoid a sweep with Minnesota now 8.5 games behind the White Sox for the AL Central division lead. Hicks is a genuine oddity: he'll serve as the opener, having started 38 games in his career but only one this season, and his velocity component (2.25 z-score, 99.2 mph) is the loudest number in this preview. Matthews counters after a strong turn — he's won each of his past four outings, most recently holding the Athletics to one run over seven innings — though his positive luck figure suggests his peripherals haven't quite caught up to the results. Chicago's tNERD (8.73) dwarfs Minnesota's (2.82), thanks to a young, cheap roster and productive bullpen against a Twins defense that's been a genuine liability. At 12.36, the gNERD clears both the historic average and today's slate, making this a solidly above-average watch, if not a marquee one.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Detroit Tigers, 10:40a

Summary

Good stuff, big enough context. Now write summary.

Tyler Glasnow is back and dealing—this is the rare Dodgers game worth setting an alarm for. The gNERD of 12.23 sits comfortably above the historic average (10.81) and today's slate, driven almost entirely by a Dodgers roster loaded with thump and a genuinely nasty Glasnow return. The big right-hander is making just his second start since missing nearly four months due to lower back spasms, and his last outing hinted at swing-and-miss stuff is intact: he allowed three runs in the first inning but struck out seven and didn't allow anything else the rest of the way. His 9.54 pNERD is built on a filthy xFIP-, so if the rust from the first-inning hiccup is gone, Detroit hitters are in trouble. Valdez, by contrast, is scuffling—8-9 with a 4.35 ERA across 26 starts this season, striking out 111 while walking 56 over 144.2 innings—and his 3.06 pNERD reflects a modest strikeout profile. The Dodgers' 8.21 tNERD (elite batting and bullpen marks) dwarfs Detroit's middling 3.66, and there's a bit of a subplot too: Shohei Ohtani was in the mix for this start before reports that he came out of his last bullpen feeling less than 100%, still undetermined if he'll pitch again this season. Add a weather delay for extra suspense, and it's a lopsided but genuinely watchable pitching mismatch.

San Diego Padres @ Tampa Bay Rays, 10:40a

Summary

Drew Rasmussen is quietly having an ace-caliber season, and that alone makes this series finale worth a look even if the Padres' offense is limping into Tropicana Field. Rasmussen enters riding a seven-game winning streak, and his 14 wins are tied for fourth-most in the Majors, backed by a sparkling walk rate and command that's earned him the highest pNERD score in today's slate at 8.21 — well above the day's average of 5.52. His xFIP- of 78 translates into a hefty positive component, and his stuff (95.7 mph average) and strike-throwing profile back up the gaudy record. Robbie Ray, by contrast, is scuffling in his first month as a Padre; he's fresh off a five-hit, two-runs-allowed no-decision against Pittsburgh, and his poor strike-throwing numbers drag his pNERD down to a near-replacement 0.97.

The Padres carry the better team NERD (9.50 vs. 4.61), thanks largely to an excellent bullpen and strong fielding marks, and San Diego is looking to avoid a series sweep after dropping an extra-innings loss to Pittsburgh-flavored funk into a shaky weekend at Tropicana Field. The overall gNERD of 11.64 sits a bit above the historical average and right in line with today's 11.15 average — a solidly watchable, if not a must-see, pitching mismatch.

Cleveland's tNERD (6.97) edges Kansas City's (4.03) thanks to a young, cheap roster and strong baserunning/fielding marks, while the Royals' bullpen (-2.39) is the biggest drag on this matchup. Overall gNERD of 11.61 sits a shade above the historical average and roughly today's middle of the pack — watchable, mostly for Messick and a shot at a sweep.

Zack Wheeler's a legit ace on paper, but his August has been a disaster, and this game mostly hinges on whether he can find the strike zone again. Wheeler's 8.59 pNERD is the headline here—his xFIP- of 73 signals a true ace, and even amid his rough month his season strikeout rate still looks like peak Wheeler. But across five starts this month he worked only 21 1/3 innings and gave up 18 earned runs, with 15 walks and no outing that reached the sixth, so don't be shocked if he's fighting his command early. Kikuchi, making his second start since coming off the 60-day injured list after missing four months with left shoulder inflammation, is a modest 4.89 pNERD arm, but his return-from-injury storyline and a fastball that's ticked up to 96 mph give it some intrigue. Team-wise, this is lopsided: Philadelphia's 5.22 tNERD is solid, buoyed by strong baserunning and bullpen work, while the Angels' 1.24 mark reflects poor fielding, baserunning, and offense. The 9.97 gNERD lands right around today's median—watchable mostly for the arms, not the standings race.

Across the mound, Max Scherzer's pNERD is essentially zero, and while he's arriving in good form, allowing two earned runs or fewer in five of his last six starts made this season, his season-long 1–7 record, 7.02 ERA, 1.54 WHIP and 36 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched tell the real story of a legend on the downslope. Detail

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 1:05p

Summary

Two of the majors' hottest arms right now, and the numbers back it up — this is the best gNERD score of the day and near the top of the season's charts. Cade Cavalli has been the Nationals' unlikely revelation, riding a stretch where he's won four straight decisions and racked up 169 strikeouts, and his 7.66 pNERD (comfortably above today's average) reflects filthy peripherals — a 77 xFIP- and mid-90s heat, even if his deliberate pace docks him a bit. Across the mound, Alcantara, in his second season back from Tommy John surgery, is returning to his Cy Young Award form, and has allowed either one or zero runs in seven of his past 10 starts — he'll also make his 198th career start, passing Ricky Nolasco for the Marlins' all-time record. Both lineups pull their weight too: Washington's offense grades out well above average on batting runs and barrel rate, while Miami counters with elite baserunning and the game's positive underlying-luck signal suggesting more offense than their results show. The Nationals' bullpen is a legitimate soft spot, so if the starters tire, expect the scoring to open up late. Overall, a rare case where the pitching matchup and the underlying team metrics are both pulling in the same direction — appointment viewing for a Saturday.

Blake Snell dominant against overmatched Detroit lineup makes this a strong watch, even if the Tigers side of the equation is mostly filler. Snell, back from elbow surgery that cost him four months, has been nails since returning—lasting exactly six innings in each of his three starts thus far while allowing only two total runs and seven hits—and his 10.26 pNERD reflects a filthy strikeout rate backed by elite peripherals (his xFIP- of 72 is comfortably one of the best marks you'll see, and today's average pitcher NERD sits at 4.59, so he's operating well above the field). Opposing him is Keider Montero, who's quietly had a solid season for Detroit but is being handled carefully after showing signs of fatigue from a career-high workload, and his modest 3.50 pNERD shows it. The Dodgers' 8.58 tNERD (well above today's 5.69 average) is built on strong batting and bullpen numbers, while Detroit's 3.33 is dragged down by shaky baserunning and fielding. At 12.83, the gNERD clears today's average of 10.35 and sits above the historical median, mostly on Snell's arm alone—worth tuning in even if Detroit's lineup looks overmatched on paper.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal returns to Comerica Park for the first time since Detroit shipped him to LA at the deadline, and that alone makes this the day's marquee watch. This is genuinely the day's best game on paper too, with a 15.59 gNERD comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, driven almost entirely by Skubal's 12.30 pNERD — elite strikeout stuff (30% K rate) paired with a minuscule xFIP- of 63. The emotional subplot writes itself: Skubal was dealt from Detroit to Los Angeles after spending his entire career with the Tigers, and now returns to face his former teammates for the first time as a visitor in what should be an emotional night. He's been sharp in LA, too — posting a 3.38 ERA with the Dodgers and striking out 11 over seven innings in his last outing. Detroit counters with journeyman Drew Anderson, a respectable 7.41 pNERD but a converted reliever who is 4-5 with a 4.09 ERA across 44 appearances, moving into the rotation only after the deadline trades of Skubal and Casey Mize. The Dodgers' 8.19 tNERD dwarfs Detroit's 3.27, and with the Dodgers freshly swept by Atlanta and the Tigers having lost 11 of their last 14, both sides have something to play for tonight beyond the reunion narrative.

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

A hard-throwing 23-year-old ace against a rookie who can't find the plate — this one's got a legitimate watchability edge. Eury Pérez brings a 98-plus mph fastball and elite whiff stuff, and he's been dealing lately: Perez is 2-0 with a 0.50 ERA in his past three starts, with 16 strikeouts and 10 walks over 18 innings. He already torched this same Nationals lineup days ago, having allowed two runs (one earned) on three hits over five innings in a 4-2 victory. His 7.91 pNERD is well above average thanks to velocity, youth, and swing-and-miss ability, though his walk tendencies and a below-average pace knock a bit off the shine. On the other side, rookie Jackson Kent is making just his fourth big-league start, and the results have been rough — Jackson Kent has walked 11 batters in just 12.1 innings, and no stats were reliable enough to generate a pNERD score, so treat him as an unknown wildcard rather than a proven arm. Both offenses actually have some juice — Washington's lineup grades out well on barrels and baserunning despite an ugly bullpen, and Miami's is young, cheap, and running hot — pushing both team NERDs near 9. Combined, the 15.55 gNERD sits comfortably above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile, making this one worth catching, mismatched arms and all.

Boston Red Sox @ New York Yankees, 4:15p

Summary

A Yankee ace with legitimate Cy Young buzz against a fading Red Sox comeback story makes this one worth clearing your evening for. Cam Schlittler has quietly turned into the story of the Yankees' season — a Walpole, Massachusetts native who's this close to a Cy Young case, and his 10.59 pNERD (among the highest scores tracked today, well above the 95th percentile) backs it up: dazzling xFIP-, plate discipline stats, and mid-upper-90s velocity from a 25-year-old who's allowed but one run over six innings against the Blue Jays last time out. Bad news for run support — the Yankees have lost four of his last five starts — but that's irrelevant to how fun he is to watch. Patrick Sandoval, by contrast, is scuffling back from 2024 elbow surgery and his pNERD sits at a middling 2.75, dragged down by a slow pace and shaky command, though he did rebound with two runs over five against the Giants. The larger plot: Boston was 14 games under .500 in June and has since ripped off a 41-14 stretch to get back into wild-card contention, adding real juice to this AL East rivalry game. Both tNERDs sit above average, with the Yankees' bullpen, barrel rate and baserunning all strong. A 14.16 gNERD lands comfortably above both the historical median and today's average — tune in for Schlittler if nothing else.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

This one's a near-must-watch, headlined by the best arm in baseball right now. Jacob Misiorowski brings a 15.57 pNERD — comfortably the highest of any pitcher in today's slate — built on a triple-digit fastball and swing-and-miss stuff that's produced a 1.68 ERA this season and two earned runs or fewer in four of his last five outings. He's not just good, he's historically good: the difference last season, though, was that Jacob Misiorowski wasn't quite Jacob Misiorowski yet, but now he's having one of the best seasons in baseball history. Manaea, by contrast, is a league-average arm on the mound (5.60 pNERD) coming off consecutive four-run outings, though his elite pace keeps him watchable in short bursts. The Brewers own the top tNERD score of the day at 9.92, fueled by strong baserunning and bullpen work, and they've dominated this series and rivalry broadly — the Milwaukee Brewers are 18-6 against the New York Mets since April 2023. The Mets counter with a solid broadcast crew and Lindor chasing a homer, but this game's appeal is really about watching a generational fastball humble a fading Mets lineup. At 18.28 gNERD, it's near the top of today's games and well above the historical average.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

A genuine ace-on-ace pitching matchup with playoff stakes attached — this one's worth clearing your schedule for. Chris Sale and Yoshinobu Yamamoto rank second and third in the NL in ERA, respectively, and both come in riding excellent underlying numbers to match, which is exactly the kind of era-defying, throwback pitching duel this sport doesn't offer often enough.

In an August series that has felt more like October baseball, a pair of star pitchers with playoff experience will highlight a game with postseason implications. The Dodgers enter riding a six-game winning streak but now try to avoid their first sweep by the Braves since May 2013, after the Braves won the first two games in dramatic fashion — 4-3 on Tuesday before Ha-Seong Kim delivered a walk-off RBI single Wednesday, his first hit since June 3. Sale's stuff is elite (10.05 pNERD, boosted by a sparkling xFIP-) even if the Braves' offense has left him hanging — he's pitched three straight quality starts in August only to lose each one as Atlanta's bats have produced just five runs across three games. Yamamoto isn't far behind at 7.97 pNERD, and he's 1-0 with 10 scoreless innings in two career outings against Atlanta, including a one-hitter in a 2-1 win last year. With gNERD at 15.94 — comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (15.60) and today's slate average (11.70) — and the Dodgers' top-tier lineup (8.26 tNERD) lurking behind Yamamoto, this has both craftsmanship and drama.

This one's a bit of a laugher-turned-slugfest series, but the pitching matchup itself won't make anyone rearrange their DVR. Baltimore and St. Louis have spent this series trading haymakers — Pete Alonso and Leody Taveras homered early Wednesday and Christian Encarnacion-Strand went 4-for-5 with a tiebreaking ninth-inning double as Baltimore blew a 7-0 lead before escaping with an 8-7 win. Houston hangs on to the top of a mediocre AL West by half a game, while New York fights for pole position in a crowded East race—so there's real stakes here, even if the on-paper numbers are lopsided. Gerrit Cole is the story: at 35 he's been pitching like peak Cole, having yielded three runs or less in nine straight starts, and he just allowed one run on four hits in six innings in a 6-1 victory in Baltimore. Detail

Texas Rangers @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

A pitching duel with real strikeout stuff on both sides makes this one worth your remote. MacKenzie Gore and Sean Burke enter as their respective teams' strikeout leaders—Gore has racked up 750 career strikeouts in 677 innings, while Burke has been a big reason the White Sox have risen up the AL standings, sitting in the top 20 of ERA, WHIP and strikeouts. Both pitchers post nearly identical pNERD marks (6.76 and 6.71) built on similarly stingy xFIP- marks around 90, giving this a nicely symmetrical mound matchup rather than a mismatch. The bigger juice comes from Chicago's tNERD (8.34), fueled by a young, bargain-payroll roster with real pop in the barrel rate—exactly the kind of scrappy, underpaid overachiever profile that makes a lineup fun to watch. Texas checks in lower (5.53) but carries a hefty positive luck score, meaning the Rangers have been underperforming their skill level and are due for better results, even as they've underperformed expectations all season, ranking 25th in runs scored and managing just seven total runs against the Angels. Add it up and you get a gNERD of 13.67, sitting comfortably above the historical average and near the top of today's slate.

Roki Sasaki brings real helium with a 97.9 mph average fastball and elite swinging-strike rate, translating to an 8.29 pNERD - well above the day's average - even though his surface numbers (5-5, 4.42 ERA) undersell the stuff. At 13.52, the gNERD sits comfortably above today's 10.83 average, so lean in for Sasaki's velocity if nothing else.

Milwaukee's runaway train of a bullpen and baserunning game rolls into Queens against a Mets team playing out the string, and while the pitching matchup won't wow anyone, the score still lands comfortably above average. The Brewers, sitting atop the NL Central at 81-51 after sweeping through the Dodgers, Mariners, and Braves, just got roughed up as May allowed seven runs on seven hits over two innings against Seattle, though his track record against these Mets is solid — a 3.38 ERA with 14 strikeouts over 18 2/3 innings, including six scoreless frames in a June win. Philadelphia Phillies @ Seattle Mariners, 1:10p

Summary

Bryan Woo has ace-level pitch quality with a mediocre record — his last outing against Milwaukee was a disaster, and the Mariners' shaky defense isn't helping his cause. Jesús Luzardo, meanwhile, is quietly having his best season, and this matchup pits two of the more electric arms in either league against each other in a series finale.

This is a well-above-average watch: the 13.09 gNERD sits comfortably above the 10.81 historical mean and lands near the top of today's slate, which ranges from 7.45 to 13.67. The pitching is doing the heavy lifting here — Luzardo's 10.72 pNERD is elite, built on a filthy 3.35 ERA, 194 strikeouts across 156 innings this year, plus mid-90s velocity and a swinging-strike rate that ranks near the top of the league. Woo's 7.57 pNERD is nothing to scoff at either, even though his surface numbers took a hit when he faced the Milwaukee Brewers and worked just 3.1 innings, surrendering six earned runs on nine hits and two walks — his xFIP suggests that outing was more bad luck than a sign of decline. Team-wise, Philadelphia's bullpen and baserunning give them the edge, while Seattle's putrid team defense (a fielding component that's one of the worst in the sample) drags their tNERD down to 2.46, even with some positive regression looming given their negative luck score. The Mariners are also chasing a series sweep after taking the first two behind strong starts, so there's a little extra juice on the line even if the marquee attraction here is arm talent rather than lineup fireworks.

Connor Prielipp, a 25-year-old lefty who returned from Tommy John surgery to make his MLB debut this year, posts a 7.13 pNERD thanks largely to his age, mid-90s velocity, and a hefty positive luck score suggesting his rough surface numbers should actually improve. J.T. Ginn, meanwhile, is basically league-average filler here (3.17 pNERD) despite Oakland treating him as their de facto ace; his last outing was rocky, allowing six hits and three runs over five innings, and he hasn't looked dominant since July 18. Watch only if you're already invested in the Prielipp redemption arc.

Detail

Boston Red Sox @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

A near-max gNERD score of 15.64 makes this the day's best watch, anchored by a red-hot Red Sox rookie and two roster-building underdogs. Payton Tolle brings a 9.74 pNERD into a start nearing the one-year anniversary of his debut, and he's been nails lately — he has won four straight decisions and is 2-0 with a 2.16 ERA in four starts this month, backed by elite strike-throwing and whiff rates that outstrip his tidy xFIP-. Miami's mystery starter (probably journeyman Tyler Phillips, who worked out of the bullpen his last time out) carries a blank pNERD, so don't expect fireworks from that side of the mound. Team-wise, the Marlins post the higher tNERD (9.35) thanks to a young, cheap roster and serious positive luck — they're underperforming their skill marks and due for better results. Boston's 7.18 tNERD leans on a strong bullpen and its own modest positive luck. Add in a fresh Rafael Devers subplot back in Boston's lineup, and this one edges out today's average gNERD of 11.48 by a wide margin.

Milwaukee Brewers @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

The best-in-baseball Brewers roll into Citi Field with a live-armed lefty on the mound, and this one's got real gNERD juice. Milwaukee sits at 81-50, MLB's best record, and comes in having taken each of their last three series against the Dodgers, Mariners, and Braves; the Mets, by contrast, own the sixth-worst record in the league and have been outscored by 40 runs this season. Kyle Harrison, whose 10.77 pNERD is well above today's field, has quietly been terrific — his xFIP- of 72 and knack for missing bats and pounding the zone are backed up by real results, including a bounce-back start where he tossed five shutout innings against Seattle, striking out eight in a 22-0 Brewers blowout. He's young (24) and pitches fast, both plusses for watchability. Opposing him is rookie Zac Thornton, who will make his 10th career start after last allowing three earned runs on seven hits in five innings against San Diego — solid enough production, though we don't have advanced metrics to grade him. Milwaukee's tNERD (10.00) is elite, driven by strong baserunning and bullpen work; the Mets are more middling. Overall gNERD of 15.54 ranks near the top of both today's slate and the historical distribution — worth carving out time for.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

Paul Skenes and a Padres bullpen that leads the league in shutting doors — this one has actual stakes and actual talent, even if the box scores haven't been cooperating lately. Skenes still owns elite peripherals (his pNERD of 10.57 is well above today's average), but Pittsburgh needs Skenes to resemble the ace he was in his first two seasons instead of the pitcher who has been pretty mortal lately, and his last outing was shaky — he lasted only 4 1/3 innings and 81 pitches, yielding four hits and three runs with four walks and five strikeouts. King is steadier than flashy, sitting at a modest pNERD of 3.46, but he's been the Padres' most dependable arm this year. San Diego's tNERD (9.93) is buoyed by a shutdown bullpen and strong fielding, both firmly above league norms, while Pittsburgh's solid baserunning gets undercut by shaky defense. The Padres are fighting for their playoff lives, and Monday's extra-inning loss to Pittsburgh only raises the tension. With a gNERD of 15.33 — comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (15.60 is close) and today's slate average of 11.48 — this is one of the better watches on the board, thanks mostly to Skenes' upside and a Padres club with real October urgency.

A hard-throwing strikeout machine against a rebuilding Angels club that's quietly figured out how to pitch a little better since firing its pitching coach — this one's worth a look mostly because of the guy on the Cleveland mound. Gavin Williams enters riding a hot second half, having just punched his 200th strikeout of the season and touching a 100.3 mph heater at the top of the zone in his last outing against San Francisco. His 12.41 pNERD is comfortably above today's average, built on elite whiff and strike rates and a mid-90s-plus fastball that has made him a pitcher with "a knack for limiting balls in play," to the point that "it's crazy that anybody touches him." Walbert Ureña, the 22-year-old on the other side, brings his own triple-digit-adjacent velocity and a tidy 6.95 pNERD, though his control still lags. The Guardians' 7.03 tNERD reflects a scrappy, contact-oriented club that has clawed back into the wild-card picture, arriving in Anaheim on a five-game winning streak and just 2.5 games out of a playoff spot. The Angels' 1.27 tNERD tells the other story — a last-place team with shaky defense and baserunning. Overall gNERD of 13.83 sits above both the historical and today's averages, making this a solid pick if you like watching a bat-missing arm work.

Tyler Glasnow's long-awaited return from a back that's been barking since May headlines a Dodgers-Braves matchup with real playoff stakes attached. Glasnow last took the mound on May 6th before back spasms shelved him for over three months; he'll come back with a track record of going 3-0 with a 2.72 ERA and 49 strikeouts over 39⅔ innings in seven starts before his absence, and his 8.75 pNERD — driven by nasty swinging-strike rates and a stingy xFIP— suggests that track record is legit, not lucky. The Dodgers arrive riding a six-game winning streak, and their 8.26 tNERD reflects a lineup that hits for both power and average, though a middling broadcast package keeps it from climbing higher. On the other side, Bryce Elder has quietly authored a bounce-back season after posting ERAs of 6.52 and 5.30 the last two campaigns, though he's "fighting through some knee stuff" according to his manager, and his modest stuff shows in a below-average 4.87 pNERD. At 13.56, the gNERD score sits comfortably above the historical average and roughly in line with today's slate, making this a solid, if not spectacular, watch.

The gNERD here sits at 10.89, right around league average both historically and for today's slate, so this isn't a must-see, but there's enough substance to make it worthwhile. Ian Seymour is the headline attraction, with a strong 8.05 pNERD driven by excellent contact management (an 87 xFIP-) and a knack for missing bats and pounding the zone; he's quietly built a 9-4 record while helping the Rays chase a division title. Jackson Jobe, on the other hand, carries no pNERD data, reflecting his up-and-down rookie season — he's shown flashes, bouncing back against the Pirates by allowing four hits and one earned run over 5.1 innings, but inconsistency remains the theme. Tampa Bay's tNERD edges Detroit's thanks to better batting output and underlying luck suggesting more runs are coming, while Detroit's roster skews toward barrel rate and payroll spend without much to show for it lately, having dropped four straight at home. Not appointment viewing, but a reasonably watchable Tuesday matchup with a real pitching mismatch worth checking in on.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

Ashcraft's electric arm makes this one worth your evening even if Robbie Ray's presence gives you pause. The Pirates' 26-year-old righty enters riding a stretch that got him an All-Star nod as a Misiorowski injury replacement, and he's been nails lately — he beat the Tigers his last time out, allowing one run on five hits while striking out four across eight innings without a walk. His 11.81 pNERD, built on elite strike-throwing and 97-mph heat, is the best pitching mark in today's slate. Ray, by contrast, is scuffling — his below-average strikeout stuff and wandering command produce a middling xFIP and the lowest pNERD on the board, though he's avoided disaster results so far. San Diego brings the juice on the other side of the ball: the Padres have won 14 of their last 18 games and sit tied for the final NL wild card spot, while Pittsburgh has dropped three straight and needs to find something on the road. The Padres' bullpen (headlined by a lights-out closer) and strong glovework push their tNERD near the top of today's games, giving this one a 14.50 gNERD that clears the historical 95th percentile.

Matthews still posts the better pNERD (6.30 vs. 1.58) thanks to plus velocity, a young age bump, and some positive luck suggesting his shiny surface numbers should actually get better, not worse. Jeffrey Springs, on the other hand, is running a 122 xFIP- for the last-place Athletics (51-80), and his component score gets dinged hard for it — his last outing (5 2/3 innings, two earned runs) was tidy, but the season-long profile isn't. Both teams are held back on the team side too: Oakland's dreadful in fielding, baserunning and bullpen, while Minnesota's own defense and bullpen woes drag down an offense that's just okay. With a gNERD of 6.63 — well below both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate average (11.15) — this is one to skip unless the standings race is dead.

New York Mets @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered from the successful searches.

A rookie sensation with a knee-buckling curveball squares off against a bullpen journeyman having a career revival, on a Chicago South Side surprise team that's quietly become one of baseball's youngest and most fun outfits. This one clears the bar for watchability, and the numbers back up the eyeball test.

Nolan McLean, the Mets' 24-year-old with what scouts already call one of the best curveballs in the league, brings a 7.98 pNERD built on a stingy xFIP- and electric stuff. He had his worst start of the season last time out, surrendering five earned runs over five innings, though he's still pitched to a 3.42 ERA in 24 starts this season. After his midseason call-up to the majors last year, he lit up stuff models en route to a sparkling ERA and WHIP, sitting mid-90s with two fastballs and a curveball that grades as one of the best in the game. Across the mound, Sean Newcomb isn't a household name but posts a respectable 5.61 pNERD, helped by a fast pace and solid contact management, even while absorbing some rough puck. The White Sox, sporting the league's youngest roster and a payroll near the bottom of MLB, still have out-produced expectations at the plate, giving this game a tNERD of 8.74 that dwarfs the Mets' 5.43. With a gNERD of 13.88, well above the historical average and near the top of today's slate, this is one worth carving out time for.

Cristopher Sánchez is having the kind of season that makes an ace's Sunday start must-watch, and this rubber-adjacent finale between two teams still fighting for playoff positioning gives it real stakes on top of the pitching. Sánchez brings a 10.09 pNERD — well above today's average — built on a strikeout-heavy, ground-ball profile that's produced a sparkling xFIP- of 61 and elite swinging-strike and strike rates; he's compiled a 2.51 ERA with 187 strikeouts and has allowed one earned run or fewer in three of his last four starts. Leahy is a serviceable middle-of-the-pack arm (5.42 pNERD) with a strong xFIP- of 88 but low whiff numbers, and he'll need to keep the ball down against a Phillies lineup fueled by Schwarber's MLB-leading power. The Phillies enter riding a seven-game winning streak, while the Cardinals have lost three of their last four games and rank near the bottom of the league offensively. Both teams carry middling tNERD scores buoyed more by bullpen and baserunning quirks than star power, so the appeal here is almost entirely Sánchez — watch for the strikeouts, not the offense. Overall gNERD of 13.68 sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, making this one of the better-watch options on the slate.

Atlanta, by contrast, is a middling 5.08 tNERD outfit still shaking off a rough season, though a hefty barrel rate suggests some thump in the lineup once the puck-luck evens out; Atlanta's batting and baserunning numbers are actually underperforming their skill level, hinting at better days ahead.

On the mound, it's a matchup of newcomers: Mahle was acquired by the Braves at the trade deadline in a deal with the Giants, his fifth team in a decade of ball. José Soriano is the headliner here, and deservedly so — his 7.01 pNERD is comfortably above average, built on mid-90s-plus velocity and a strong SwStr% that props up an xFIP- in the low 90s. Soriano has posted a 2.22 ERA over his first three starts with the Blue Jays, giving Toronto a workhorse who should keep this competitive deep into the game. Carlos Rodón, by contrast, grades out as a modestly below-average pull at 3.65 pNERD, with a strike rate that lags the league; still, he carries a 3.55 ERA over his last five starts, and interestingly, the Blue Jays have been destroying lefty pitchers lately, batting .365 with 6.4 runs per game over the last five games — a matchup wrinkle worth watching. On the team side, the Yankees' 7.96 tNERD is buoyed by strong barrel rate and baserunning marks, while Toronto's fielding is its calling card. A gNERD of 10.94 sits right around the historical middle but above today's slate average — solidly watchable, not appointment viewing.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Milwaukee Brewers, 1:10p

Summary

This one has it all: two of the best pitchers in baseball, a real division-race stake, and a preview of a potential October rematch. The gNERD of 20.64 is the top mark of today's slate and among the highest scores in the dataset's history, and once you see the details, it's not hard to see why.

Misiorowski is the headline act, sporting a pNERD of 15.87 that leads the league today, built on a triple-digit fastball (100.7 mph average), a filthy swinging-strike rate, and an xFIP- of 48 that's simply absurd. He's overmatching opponents with a 100-plus mph fastball and a knee-buckling cutter, compiling a big-league-high 210 strikeouts. Across the mound, 37-year-old Sale is no slouch either, still pumping mid-90s heat with elite command, good for a 9.84 pNERD. The pitchers with the major leagues' top two ERAs will go head to head as the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves visit Jacob Misiorowski and the NL Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers, with some suggesting it's quite possibly a pitching preview of Game 1 of an NL Division Series matchup. The Brewers' tNERD of 10.14 is buoyed by strong baserunning and bullpen work, giving this one both star power and team quality — a rare slate-topper worth clearing your schedule for.

Two under-.500 teams with surprisingly lively NERD profiles make this one worth a look, even if the standings suggest otherwise. Washington enters on a skid — the Nationals are trying to avoid losing eight of their last 10 games and have lost five of their last six — while Miami is scuffling too, fresh off being swept by the Phillies in three close games, though the Marlins are technically still in the playoff chase, four games behind the Padres for the final NL Wild Card spot. Both clubs post tNERD scores around 9.1, well above the historic norm, thanks to young rosters, modest payrolls and (for Miami) a Batting Luck score of 1.60 suggesting their offense should be scoring more than it has. On the mound, Brad Lord has been steady all year — a 4.04 ERA, 1.25 WHIP, 8.23 K/9 over 62.1 innings — while Ryan Gusto, still hunting his first win, has quietly turned things around, posting a 3.07 ERA through three starts in August. Neither arm is dominant, but both are solid enough to keep this from turning into a slugfest. With a gNERD of 14.79, well above today's average, this one's worth a spot on the watch list.
